attribution.note: Marcus directly states and endorses the legislative assessment.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the broad technology-industry scope and retrospective endpoint without importing an AI-only restriction.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary and fair. Weighing substantive enacted constraints more heavily than proposals respects the wording, while allowing limited exceptions. The unspecified starting point makes older legislation relevant.

evidence.note: Contemporary reporting supports limited progress on major AI regulation as of May 15. It covers only part of the industry and does not establish developments through June 5.
The broad privacy framework remained a draft near the statement date. Committee activity demonstrates some progress but does not establish enacted obligations.
Existing children's privacy law imposed substantive consent, security, and deletion duties on covered online operators. These qualify the cumulative claim, although their coverage is limited.
Congress enacted enforceable marketplace verification and disclosure obligations effective before the statement. These are concrete constraints, though confined to marketplace activity.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports limited progress toward broad AI and comprehensive privacy regulation. However, existing children's privacy duties and enacted marketplace obligations establish substantive congressional constraints in specific areas. The broad characterization understates those accomplishments; the evidence does not establish comprehensive industry-wide reform.
